clue.text: Recall sacred syllable as if lacking in spirit

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the word is taken back from end to start

parts.note: om is the sacred syllable chanted in Hindu and Buddhist practice
'As if!' and 'pish!' are both scornful exclamations of disbelief

explanation.surface: Someone chanting a holy syllable half-heartedly, as though their heart isn't in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Mopish describes someone moping, dejected and listless, with no spirit.

clue.text: Male sycophant overlooking leader's mistake

indicators.note: overlooking its leader means ignoring the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for male
a suck-up is a toady or flatterer

explanation.surface: A toadying man's failure to notice his boss amounts to an error.
explanation.walkthrough: The sycophant loses its first letter S before the M of male is put in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A muck-up is an informal noun for a botched job or blunder.

clue.text: Self-righteous churchgoers lifting up hearts? Hearts of vain deacons

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifting up the hearts symbol moves that one letter higher in the word

parts.note: the parish is the body of people attending a local church

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central part, so only the middle letters are kept

parts.note: the two central letters of vain
the central letter of deacons

explanation.surface: Smug congregants singing 'Lift up your hearts' while their deacons are vain at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: H is the card abbreviation for hearts; in the parish it moves up from last place to second. The Pharisees are the Gospel byword for sanctimony.
explanation.definitionFit: Pharisaic, after the Pharisees, means hypocritically self-righteous, a sanctimonious show of observance.

clue.text: What's left in eye by end of nap?

definitions.text: What's left in eye by end of nap?

parts.note: surface reading: a riddle about something that remains in the eye
setter's reading: the crust that gathers in the corners of the eyes during a snooze, which shares its name with the snooze itself

explanation.walkthrough: The gritty deposit found in the corner of the eye on waking is called by the same word as the rest that produced it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleep is the everyday name for the dried mucus found at the corners of the eyes after resting.

clue.text: This is well done sentimentality in commercial book

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the advert word, wrapped by it

parts.note: an ad is a commercial
goo is mawkish sentiment
Job is a book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: Praise for a soppy advertising campaign book.
explanation.definitionFit: 'A good job' is the phrase of praise someone says to mean that a task has been well done.

clue.text: Tips from this analytic strategy help suffering

definitions.text: Tips from this analytic strategy help suffering

indicators.note: suffering words are in a bad way, knocked out of their normal shape
tips are the front ends of words, so the initial letters are taken

parts.note: first letters of this and analytic
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice from a psychoanalytic approach on helping those in distress.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a therapeutic strategy that helps the suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: Gestalt therapy is a psychotherapy focused on present awareness, a treatment to help people in distress.

clue.text: Fine Oscar legend departs Love Island

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO alphabet
the legend of a map is its key
d. is the timetable abbreviation for departs
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
a key is a low island, as in the Florida Keys

explanation.surface: A screen-legend Oscar winner quits the reality show Love Island.
explanation.walkthrough: Love Island is a British dating reality TV show, which disguises the two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Okey-dokey is a jokey form of OK, said to mean all right or agreed.

clue.text: One's entertained by junior dancer

indicators.note: a guest entertained by a host is held inside the host's home

parts.note: Jr is the abbreviation for junior
I've: one = I and 's as a contraction of has

explanation.surface: Someone being looked after by a younger dancer.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'has', so 'one has' becomes I've.
explanation.definitionFit: A jiver is one who dances the jive, the lively swing-era style.

clue.text: Degree of interest when dons lecture

indicators.note: to don is to put on, so the scolding word is worn around the other

parts.note: to lecture someone is to berate them
as = when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: How keen are students when university fellows give a talk?
explanation.walkthrough: Dons look like university teachers, which fits lecture neatly, but the word is a verb meaning puts on.
explanation.definitionFit: The base rate is the central bank's benchmark lending figure, the level of interest charged.

clue.text: Anonymous power brokers recovering having lost 500 concerning, unknown claims

indicators.note: having lost something means it has been dropped from the preceding word

parts.note: a patient on the mend is recovering
D is the Roman numeral for 500
re means about, concerning
y is an algebraic unknown
a lawsuit is a legal claim

explanation.surface: Faceless fixers bouncing back after a costly series of legal disputes.
explanation.definitionFit: Men in grey suits is an idiom for the faceless establishment figures who wield influence behind the scenes.

clue.text: Unrelenting Seles aces shot

indicators.note: something shot is ruined or wrecked, so the letters are broken up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Tennis star Monica Seles keeps hitting service winners without letup.
explanation.walkthrough: Shot looks like a tennis stroke, but it means broken.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceaseless means never stopping, a synonym of relentless.

clue.text: The King's section of trunk, not initially packed

indicators.note: not initially means the first letter of the next word is left out

parts.note: the pelvis is the bony base of the torso
first letter of packed

explanation.surface: Part of a royal's luggage trunk has been left unpacked.
explanation.walkthrough: Trunk suggests luggage but is the torso; the letter removed is the opening one of packed.
explanation.definitionFit: Elvis Presley is known as the King of Rock and Roll.

clue.text: Academic's body that's found near end of whodunit

indicators.note: found near the end tells us the letters sit, concealed, towards the finish of the next word

parts.note: the letters just before its final t

explanation.surface: A don's corpse discovered in the last chapter of a murder mystery.
explanation.walkthrough: Body tempts one towards a corpse, but here it means an institution.
explanation.definitionFit: A university, informally shortened, is an institution or body of academics.

clue.text: Mountain native, ignoring case of gooseflesh, interrupts a wolf

indicators.note: something that interrupts breaks in, so it sits inside the other piece

parts.note: per = a, as in 'ten pounds a head'

indicators.note: ignoring the case means dropping the outside pair of letters of the following word

parts.note: a highlander is a native of mountain country
outer letters of gooseflesh

explanation.surface: A shivering hill-dweller breaks in on a wolf.
explanation.walkthrough: Wolf is the slang sense: a man who chases women.
explanation.definitionFit: A wolf, in slang, is a predatory womaniser, which is what a philanderer is.

clue.text: Villain's unsettled, breaking rib

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it

parts.note: to rib and to rag both mean to tease
TBA, to be arranged, describes something not yet settled

explanation.surface: A shaken crook has cracked a rib.
explanation.walkthrough: Rib looks like a bone but is the verb meaning to mock.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratbag is Australian and British slang for a rogue or nasty person.

clue.text: Impenetrable language of boyfriend Fleabag chucked

indicators.note: things chucked about land any old way, mixed up

parts.note: BF is texting shorthand for boyfriend
taken as written

explanation.surface: The confusing words Fleabag used when dumping her boyfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: Fleabag is the TV comedy heroine, but here just a string of letters; chucked means dumped in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Bafflegab is jargon-filled gobbledegook meant to confuse, unintelligible verbiage.

clue.text: Date Kate?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to escort someone on a romantic evening
second meaning, cryptic: the name is the four-letter verb for seize with its letters put out of order, the question mark flagging the wordplay

explanation.walkthrough: The answer phrase both means to date and, read as an instruction, describes how Kate is formed: its four letters rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone out is to escort them on a romantic outing.

clue.text: Speaker's spoken about a wild riot

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word wraps the rest

parts.note: oral means spoken

indicators.note: a wild crowd is out of control, so its letters run riot

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A speaker has reported on an out-of-control disturbance.
explanation.definitionFit: Oratorial is the adjective relating to an orator, a public speaker, so it means belonging to one.

clue.text: Government department has first-class harvest stored inside hopper, maybe

indicators.note: things stored inside a place are kept within its walls

parts.note: the MoD is the UK Ministry of Defence
A is the top grade
a crop is a harvest

explanation.surface: A ministry has a fine crop held in a grain hopper.
explanation.walkthrough: Hopper looks like a grain bin; it is an animal that hops, and 'maybe' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Macropods are the kangaroo family of marsupials, which move by hopping.

clue.text: Enemy for each liberal

indicators.note: liberal means free and loose, so the letters are rearranged freely

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Every left-leaning politician is an opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: An arch-foe is a chief adversary, the main enemy.

clue.text: Prime colour around grass borders

indicators.note: the grass word borders the other, lying on both sides of it

parts.note: hay is dried grass

indicators.note: turned around means facing the opposite way

parts.note: to dye is to colour

explanation.surface: A leading paint shade surrounds the edges of the lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: One's heyday is one's prime, the period of greatest success.

clue.text: Put time into pigpen to get ham

indicators.note: put into means placed inside something else

parts.note: a sty is a pig enclosure
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Spend time in a pig enclosure to produce gammon.
explanation.walkthrough: Ham suggests pork, natural beside a pigpen, but here it is an adjective for over-the-top acting.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagey means theatrical and exaggerated, as a ham actor's performance is.

clue.text: Small jolly dogs discover driver's alert

parts.note: to rumble someone is to find them out
S is the abbreviation for small
a jolly is a pleasure outing, a trip

explanation.surface: Little cheerful hounds sniff something out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dogs' is a verb meaning follows, so the small trip comes after the discovery word. Rumble and jolly are both British informal: to be found out, and a jaunt.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumble strip is a ridged road surface that vibrates to warn motorists.

clue.text: First-rate tango's intended

parts.note: in slang, mean means excellent, as in 'plays a mean guitar'
tango is T in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: An excellent tango is what was planned.
explanation.definitionFit: Meant is the past participle of mean, purposed or planned.

clue.text: Store up hydrogen for lab?

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: the Co-op is a British chain of stores
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen

explanation.surface: Keep some hydrogen in reserve for the laboratory.
explanation.walkthrough: Lab looks like a laboratory, natural next to hydrogen; it is a Labrador, and the question mark flags it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A pooch is an informal word for a dog, and a Labrador is one breed.

clue.text: Anything that hurts won't in the end

parts.note: ow is the cry when something hurts

indicators.note: in the end points to the closing letter of the word only

parts.note: final letter of won't

explanation.surface: Nothing painful will happen ultimately.
explanation.walkthrough: Owt is northern English dialect for anything, as in 'owt or nowt'.
explanation.definitionFit: Owt is a Yorkshire dialect word meaning something or anything.

clue.text: Crash parking Golf, having raced in

indicators.note: having something in means holding it inside

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
ran = raced
golf is G in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A car accident after speeding into a golf car park.
explanation.walkthrough: Prang is British slang for a minor car crash. The final 'in' completes the container indicator with 'having'.
explanation.definitionFit: A prang is a colloquial word for a collision or bump in a vehicle.

clue.text: Confession of policeman during head of gang's collapsing

parts.note: a policeman admitting 'I'm plod'; plod is British slang for a police officer
in = during, as in 'in the night'

indicators.note: 'head of' keeps only the first letter of 'gang'

parts.note: first letter of gang

explanation.surface: A cop owns up while the gang boss's empire is falling apart.
explanation.walkthrough: Plod, from Mr Plod in the Noddy books, is British slang for the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Imploding means caving in on itself, falling inwards.

clue.text: Records listened to show the age of a singer

indicators.note: listened to means we go by how the words are heard rather than spelt

parts.words: show the age of a singer
parts.note: date = show the age of, plus a + bass, a low singer

explanation.surface: Archive recordings were heard to reveal how old a vocalist is.
explanation.definitionFit: A database is an organised store of records held on a computer.

clue.text: Distant and cold, like the Lake District

parts.note: C is the tap abbreviation for cold
the Lake District is a mountainous national park in north-west England

explanation.surface: A description of the remote, bleak northern English fells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distant and cold' looks like a double definition, but cold is only the letter C.
explanation.definitionFit: A chilly manner is aloof and unfriendly, so distant fits it as a synonym.
